tasks.title: A1: a well-formed dungeon id that names no dungeon reports NotFound and stops saves
acceptance: When `GetDungeonDetailQuery` returns null, `LoadDungeonAsync` (base `DungeonDetailViewModel.cs:172-181`) sets the loaded identifier back to `Guid.Empty`. Evidence: a test drives `ApplyQueryAttributes` with `ShellRoutes.IdQueryKey` mapped to a well-formed `Guid`, the substituted `AppDispatcher` returns null for that query, and the test awaits `LoadTask`. It then asserts that `DungeonId == Guid.Empty`.

In that same null-query state, `ErrorMessage` is non-null. It is assigned as `ResultMessage.ForFailure(<a new static readonly Result>)` with `ErrorCategory.NotFound`, declared beside `UnusableNavigationIdResult` (base `DungeonDetailViewModel.cs:22-24`). The wording does not say the navigation request was malformed: the id was well formed, and the same branch is reached from `ReloadAsync` (base `:158-159`). Evidence: a test asserting `ErrorMessage` is non-null after `LoadTask` completes, plus the diff for the wording.

After a null-query load, executing `Header.SaveCommand` dispatches nothing. Evidence: a test asserting that the substituted dispatcher received no `SendAsync` call of any overload. Configure the substitute's `SendAsync` to return a completed `Result.Success()`, so that under the injection below the test fails on this assertion and not on awaiting a null `Task`.

Reload path, dungeon deleted between commands: a load returns a DTO, `Header.SaveCommand` succeeds, and the reload that save triggers (`DungeonHeaderViewModel.cs:96`, through `ReloadAsync`) returns null. After that, `DungeonId == Guid.Empty` and `ErrorMessage` is non-null. Evidence: a test asserting both values once the save command's task completes.

Continuing that reload-path test: a second `Header.SaveCommand` dispatches nothing more, so the dispatcher received exactly one `SendAsync` across the whole test. Evidence: a received-call count assertion in that test.

Control, which must pass both with and without the injection below: when the query returns a DTO, `DungeonId` equals that DTO's id, `ErrorMessage` stays null after the load, and `Header.SaveCommand` dispatches exactly one command.

Demonstrated discrimination (test.md, Coverage: 'A test is shown able to fail'). Injection `a1-null-branch`: restore the body of `LoadDungeonAsync` to its base text (`:174-180`, no null branch). Then do the following once for this injection. Save a pre-injection copy of the file in your scratch directory and apply the injection. Run `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DungeonDetailViewModelMissingDungeonTests"` and save the full output to `<scratch>/inject-a1-null-branch.log`. Restore the file from the copy and prove the restore with `cmp` against the copy. Re-run the same command into `<scratch>/inject-a1-null-branch-restored.log`. The report gives both absolute log paths. From each log it quotes the line naming the failed/passed/total counts and the failing test names. Every test above except the control must be red under the injection, and the control must be green. If a named test stays green, report that with the log rather than adjusting the criterion.

The new tests live in `DungeonMaster.App.Tests`. Its `InternalsVisibleTo` (`src/DungeonMaster.App/AssemblyInfo.cs:3`) lets the test use the real `ShellRoutes.IdQueryKey` (`Services/Navigation/ShellRoutes.cs:19`) and not a copied `"id"` literal. `FloorReorderCommandArgsTests.cs:92` is the precedent for a substituted `AppDispatcher`. The XML documentation on `LoadDungeonAsync` (base `:161-170`) and the `ApplyQueryAttributes` parameter remarks (base `:105-109`) are true after the change. `LoadDungeonAsync`'s docs state the not-found outcome: identifier cleared, error reported, editing refused.

tasks.title: A5 + A6: non-finite zoom is rejected in ApplyZoom; OnMapCanvasHandlerChanged is guarded from its first statement (mixed-indent line separable at Gate 2)
acceptance: A new `internal static` class in `src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/ZoomLevelGuard.cs`, namespace `DungeonMaster.App.Views.DungeonDetail` (precedent `DrawSessionResultGuard.cs:3,10`), maps a current zoom level and a requested raw level to the next zoom level. A non-finite raw value returns the current level unchanged, following the finiteness precedents `CanvasPoint` and `FloorReorderNearest.cs:155`. A finite raw value gets exactly the base `ApplyZoom` treatment (`DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:516-520`): snap to 1.0 inside `ZoomSnapThreshold` (0.05, base `:53`), then clamp to [0.25, 4.0].

`ApplyZoom` (base `:514-523`) takes the zoom level it assigns from that guard, so the zoom buttons (base `:508-512`), the Windows wheel (base `:618`) and the MacCatalyst pinch (base `:632`) all pass through it. The pinch line still calls `ApplyZoom`. Evidence: the diff.

Tests in `src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/Views/ZoomLevelGuardTests.cs` show that a raw value of `float.NaN` returns the current level. The current level is one that is neither 1.0, 0.25 nor 4.0, so an unguarded snap or clamp cannot coincide with it.
Tests show that a raw value of `float.PositiveInfinity` returns that same current level. Without the guard it would clamp to 4.0.
Tests show that a raw value of `float.NegativeInfinity` returns that same current level. Without the guard it would clamp to 0.25.
Preserved behaviour, a control that must pass both with and without the injection below: a finite in-range raw value outside the snap band (for example 2.0) is returned unchanged.
Preserved behaviour, control: a finite raw value inside the snap band (for example 1.03) returns 1.0.
Preserved behaviour, control: a finite raw value above 4.0 returns 4.0.
Preserved behaviour, control: a finite raw value below 0.25 returns 0.25.

Demonstrated discrimination (test.md, Coverage). Injection `a5-isfinite`: delete the finiteness check from the guard. Then do the following once for this injection. Save a pre-injection copy of `ZoomLevelGuard.cs` and apply the injection. Run `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ZoomLevelGuardTests"` into `<scratch>/inject-a5-isfinite.log`. Restore from the copy, prove the restore with `cmp`, and re-run into `<scratch>/inject-a5-isfinite-restored.log`. Quote each log's count line and failing test names. All three non-finite tests must be red and all four finite controls green.

The report states whether the solution build compiled the `net10.0-maccatalyst` target of `DungeonMaster.App` and quotes the build output line showing it. If that target was not built, it says so. The MacCatalyst pinch path is not executable on this machine, and the report does not claim it was exercised.

In `OnMapCanvasHandlerChanged` (base `:533-560`), `DetachScrollZoom()` and `AttachScrollZoom()` (base `:535-536`) execute inside the `try` (base `:548`), and no statement executes before the `try`. Evidence: the diff.

It names the scroll-zoom attach/detach as well as the image preload, or reads as a canvas-preparation failure that covers both (backend.md, Error handling: 'Include the operation … in the failure').
